primary_process_null: independent Brownian trajectories on exact observed system trees with all families and traits sharing identical sigma2

comparisons.family_repeatability: Observed log(K) family conditional repeatability versus the null distribution of the identical REML fit, one-sided high
comparisons.rank_portability: Observed LOFO within-family K rank prediction SSE gain versus the matched Brownian-null distribution, one-sided high
comparisons.absolute_portability: Observed held-out-family log(K) absolute prediction gain versus the matched Brownian-null distribution, one-sided high
comparisons.reversal: Observed weighted pair-order reversal versus null distribution, two-sided; 50% itself is not evidence for adaptive rewiring

outcome_categories.strong: Observed rank portability AND conditional family repeatability exceed their individual 97.5% null quantiles on BOTH prune and S3. Label as beyond identical-BM null on these K metrics; no causal ecology claim.
outcome_categories.partial: At least one metric exceeds its null 97.5% bound but strong condition is not met; report which axis/metric and source graph support it.
outcome_categories.not_supported: No rank-portability or family repeatability metric exceeds its null 97.5% bound. Retain descriptive estimator differences, do not claim process heterogeneity.
outcome_categories.insufficient: Missing or invalid fixed graph, unmatched K calculations, <61/64 family-null valid replicates, or incomplete K-null data; no scientific verdict.

multiple_testing_caution: These contrasts are post-outcome exploratory; quantile thresholds are descriptive calibration markers, not a preregistered family-wise error guarantee.
limits: A Brownian-null exceedance may arise from non-Brownian processes, unmodeled trait covariance, measurement error or data-source artifacts rather than adaptive reallocation.
Same-rate Brownian null is one reference process and not evidence of all alternative processes being excluded.
No refit, source filter or metric change after inspecting process-null results.
Do not treat observed 40-50% reversal as by itself a discovery.
